recipes.name: Chocolate Pudding Fudge Cake
ingredients_raw: 1 (18.25 ounce) package devil's food cake mix
1 (3.9 ounce) package instant chocolate pudding mix

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease and flour a 10-inch Bundt pan.
Beat cake mix, sour cream, milk, oil, water, eggs, and pudding mix in a large bowl with an electric mixer for 4 minutes. Mix in 2 cups chocolate chips. Pour batter into the prepared pan.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean, 40 to 50 minutes. Cool in the pan for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.
Meanwhile, melt remaining 1 cup chocolate chips and butter in a double boiler or the microwave. Stir glaze until smooth, then drizzle over the cooled cake.

raw_recipe.headline: Chocolate Pudding Fudge Cake
raw_recipe.description: Try this chocolate Bundt cake recipe for a moist and irresistible cake made with cake mix, chocolate pudding mix, chocolate chips, and sour cream.

review.reviewBody: This cake is excellent. It's rich, moist and intensely chocolate. I tweaked the recipe slightly and used 2 cups of mini chips in the batter instead of the regular chocolate chips, substituted 1/2 cup Kahlua for the water, and used a BC Chocolate Fudge cake mix instead of Devil's Food. As most reviewers discovered, it takes about an hour to bake and as a matter of fact, I think mine took longer. I made a Chocolate Kahlua Glaze instead of the one in the recipe.

I'm a chocolate lover and this cake is definitely for chocoholics. I followed the recipe to a tee and it was absolutely delicious. I was a little nervous because the cake mix that I used was 15 oz vs 18 oz as the recipe calls for but it came out perfect. I dredged the chocolate chips in flour before adding to the cake batter so they wouldn't all drop to the bottom of the cake. I also cooked it in a 9 x 13 pan as I didn't have a bundt pan and ended up cooking it for 45 mins and it was perfect.

I definitely liked it. It’s a nice dense pudding cake. I used plain Greek yogurt (no lactose) instead of sour cream, almond oil instead of vegetable oil, 1 cup water, and left out the chocolate chips. Cooking times vary by humidity, elevation, and oven. I tend to bake about 2/3 of time. Afterwards, I do a toothpick check every few minutes for perfection. Used a dusting of powdered sugar, caramel drizzle, and topped with CocoWhip by So Delicious (whipped coconut cream without lactose), and a scoop of Breyer’s lactose free vanilla ice cream. It was a winner for the family holiday!

I love this chocolate cake! Has anyone ever tried doing a vanilla version? I have mine in the oven right now. The vanilla cake mix calls for less milk so I used a little less and I used white chocolate chips. I make my own icing instead of the glaze and I will do the same with the vanilla. I guess we'll see how it turns out! Oh, and I also use 2 9" round cake pans and cut the time to about 35 min.

This was AMAZING! I turned it into Black Forest Cake for my best friends Birthday. Only change I made was that I used mini choc chips.
I made it in 2 round cake pans and made sure I cooked it so it was alllmost cooked, but just a little gooey still. I let it cool completely and cut each round in half so that I had 4 round flat chunks. I put a can of Cherry Pie Filling between the top layers, and one between the bottom layers, and a layer of whipping cream in the middle layer. I iced it in whipping cream and dusted it with coco powder and let it set in the fridge for about 6 hours before serving it. It was TO DIE FOR!

I've been making it 3x a year for 25 years. I stopped frosting it, instead sprinkle the gold flakes on top. I used 1/2 cup instant milk with 7/8 cup water, a 3.9 oz box pudding. I bake for 60 minutes at 350F. Everything else was as written. Let it sit overnight before serving. Good warmed up with vanilla ice cream.

I made this into cupcakes. It yielded about 27 cupcakes that I baked for 22-25 minutes depending on size. I did not use the glaze. Serve them warm with some ice cream...the chocolate chips melt and it's SO good! I also used 3 oz sour cream, and 13 oz milk as that's what I had on hand. They were light and airy and delicious! I didn't ice them, but if I did I was thinking a whipped cream or cream cheese icing would be good.

I do not always put the chocolate chips in but when I do I use mini chips. I do not use the glaze in this recipe, but rather I use a chocolate fudge buttercream frosting and it is MAGNFIQUE! I've won dessert competitions with my mods.

My daughter and I loved the recipe. My husband thought it was slightly too gooey and too dense for his taste. It was pretty wet in texture the first time I made it, but the second day was fantastic. I did make it a second time, but this time used 2/3 cup sour cream and 1 1/4 cup water. It turned out great. Not as gooey, more cakey, but still dense and delicious. I used a traditional ganache frosting made with heavy cream and chocolate chips. VERY GOOD!

Incredibly simple recipe! Made two to take to work! Only changes I made were substituting 1/2 cup of amaretto liqueur for the water. And I added 1/8 tsp. Salt and 1 tsp. Vanilla Extract. They look great! I can't wait to try it with the ganache.
The store was out of Devils food cake so I substituted a triple chocolate fudge cake mix by betty crocker . Holy cow, what a cake

I love this recipe and have been baking it for years! I've tried several from-scratch chocolate bundt cake recipes, but this one with a cake mix is just so much better! I actually use half mini semi-sweet chocolate chips and half regular-size milk chocolate chips in the batter. For the frosting, I actually melt a can of canned chocolate frosting and drizzle it over the top. . .even easier and just as yummy!

I made this for my husband for Valentine's Day. It sounded really good on paper. However, when I made it, it was not so great. I bought a brand new bundt pan to use for this cake. I wonder if the pan might have been at least part of the problem. Despite greasing and flouring the pan, the cake stuck like crazy. I ended up taking it out in chunks. I then glued the chunks back together with some of the glaze. It worked okay, but didn't look as good as it could have. The taste was okay enough, but nothing special. I'm an experienced home cook and baker. Definitely not saying I couldn't make a mistake, but I don't know what it would have been. I followed the recipe to the letter. I'm disappointed although Hubby tells me the cake is "pretty good" and he WILL eat it. He's a big chocoholic so I'm sure he will LOL Sorry it didn't work out real well but I thank you anyway for posting the recipe.
Incredible!

I thought I had done something wrong, the batter was very thin because of all the liquid in it. And my regular oven was not working so I had to cook it in my convection-microwave oven. It was for a birthday so I was nervous, but it came out great and the flavor was really chocolaty! I will make it again and bake it in the convection oven!

What a disaster!! I had to bake it for an hour and 5 minutes. It raised up beautifully, however 10 minutes after I took it out of the oven, it fell down about half. Not a great recipe. Won't be making it again.
Yummmmm 😋

Really easy recipe. I used the butter flavor chocolate cake mix because it was on sale and it was delicious. Even without the glaze this is a simple and moist cake. Cook for the full time indicated and add a couple of tablespoons flour for high-altitudes. I used the Pam baking spray with flour and the cake came out of the pan easily.
Love this recipe so very moist!
I swapped the cake mix and pudding for vanilla. This is a rich dessert that quickly satisfies a sweet tooth.
